identification_strategy: One-line: EVENT_STUDY — treatment = birth of first child, control = pre-birth period; shock/instrument/cutoff = year of first child birth
conclusion_detail: The study finds large and persistent child penalties in earnings for women across different countries.
main_effect: Long-run child penalties range from 21% in Denmark to 61% in Germany.
key_robustness: Comparison across countries using the same empirical approach
Consideration of public policies and gender norms
notes: The study uses high-quality panel data and consistent methodology across countries, but cultural and policy differences may introduce unobserved heterogeneity.
